title: Jerome on Hosea 1:2
body: “Hosea speaks many times of Ephraim, of Samaria, of Joseph, of Jezreel, of a wife of whoredoms and of children of whoredoms, of an adulteress shut up within the chamber of her husband, sitting for a long time in widowhood and in the garb of mourning, awaiting the time when her husband will return to her.”
author: Jerome, Letter 53, to Paulinus
bodyEs: “Oseas habla muchas veces de Efraín, de Samaria, de José, de Jezreel, de una mujer de fornicaciones y de hijos de fornicaciones, de una adúltera encerrada en la cámara de su marido, sentada largo tiempo en viudez y con vestido de luto, esperando el tiempo en que su marido vuelva a ella.”

title: John Chrysostom on Hosea 2:23
body: “Here to prevent their saying, that you are deceiving us here with specious reasoning, he calls Hosea to witness, who crieth and saith, "I will call them My people, who were not My people." (Hos.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans
bodyEs: “Aquí, para impedir que digan que los engañas con un razonamiento especioso, llama por testigo a Oseas, que clama y dice: "Diré á Lo-ammi: Pueblo mío tú." (Os.”

title: John Chrysostom on Hosea 4:2
body: “Henceforward, what consolation shall there be for us? He called us to Heaven, and we have thrust ourselves down to hell.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on John and Hebrews
bodyEs: “En adelante, ¿qué consuelo habrá para nosotros? Nos llamó al cielo, y nosotros nos hemos empujado al infierno.”

title: John Chrysostom on Hosea 4:8
body: “This is hospitality, this is truly to do it for God's sake. But if you give orders with pride, though you bid him take the first place, it is not hospitality, it is not done for God's sake.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon
bodyEs: “Esta es hospitalidad, esto es hacerlo de verdad por causa de Dios. Pero si das órdenes con orgullo, aunque le mandes tomar el primer lugar, no es hospitalidad, no se hace por causa de Dios.”

title: John Chrysostom on Hosea 6:5
body: “How is it "for them?" How is it "their glory?" It is because God so loved them, as to give even the Son for them, and to afflict His servants for them: for it was in order that they might attain so many blessings, that Paul was in prison.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon
bodyEs: “¿Cómo es "por ellos"? ¿Cómo es "gloria de ellos"? Es porque Dios los amó tanto que dio incluso al Hijo por ellos, y afligió a sus siervos por ellos: porque fue para que alcanzaran tantas bendiciones que Pablo estuvo en la cárcel.”

title: John Chrysostom on Hosea 6:6
body: “Either then we may say this, or that his meaning is for those who give to be also joined closely to those who retire, and not merely to give without sympathy, but in pity and condescension, bowing down and grieving with the needy.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians
bodyEs: “O podemos decir esto, o que su sentido es que los que dan se unan también de cerca a los que se retiran, y no solo den sin compasión, sino con piedad y condescendencia, inclinándose y doliéndose con el necesitado.”

title: John Chrysostom on Hosea 12:10
body: “And well did he begin thus, "At sundry times and in divers manners," for he points out that not even the prophets themselves saw God; nevertheless, the Son saw Him. For the expressions, "at sundry times and in divers manners" are the same as "in different ways." "For I" (saith He) "have multiplied visions, and used similitudes by the ministry of the Prophets." ( Hos.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on John and Hebrews
bodyEs: “Y bien empezó así: "en diversos tiempos y de diversas maneras", porque señala que ni los profetas mismos vieron a Dios; sin embargo, el Hijo lo vio. Porque las expresiones "en diversos tiempos y de diversas maneras" son lo mismo que "de distintos modos". "Y hablado he á los profetas, y yo aumenté la profecía, y por mano de los profetas puse semejanzas." (Os.”
